queries: WITH r AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS a FROM film GROUP BY rating), t1 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS m1 FROM r), c1 AS (SELECT r.rating, r.a FROM r CROSS JOIN t1 WHERE r.a > t1.m1), t2 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS m2 FROM c1), c2 AS (SELECT c1.rating, c1.a FROM c1 CROSS JOIN t2 WHERE c1.a > t2.m2) SELECT AVG(c2.a) AS mean_of_remaining_avg_lengths, AVG(c2.a - t1.m1) AS avg_above_first_average, AVG(c2.a - t2.m2) AS avg_above_first_cut_mean FROM c2 CROSS JOIN t1 CROSS JOIN t2

assumptions.assumption: The first 'average' is the unweighted mean of the five per-rating average lengths. This matches the later phrase 'mean of their own average lengths'. Each film length is averaged per rating, and NULL lengths are ignored by AVG.

'That first average' (the baseline for the second measure) is the first-cut threshold, i.e. the mean of all ratings' averages. 'The mean of the ratings that passed the first cut' is the second threshold. The final mean is taken over the ratings that pass the second cut.

alternatives.interpretation: The first 'average' is the overall average length across all films (each film weighted equally), not the mean of the per-rating averages.

assumptions.assumption: The first 'average' benchmark is the unweighted mean of the five per-rating average lengths, which matches the later phrase 'mean of their own average lengths'. It is not the film-level average.
The second cut uses the mean of the average lengths of the ratings that passed the first cut. Ratings must be strictly greater than each benchmark. AVG ignores NULL lengths.

alternatives.interpretation: The first benchmark is the overall average length across all films, with each film weighted equally, instead of the mean of the rating averages.

assumptions.assumption: The first 'average' is the overall average length of all films with a non-null length (AVG(length) over film), not the mean of the per-rating averages. 'Longer than average' and 'the mean of their own average lengths' are worded as two different benchmarks, so I read the first as the overall film average.

'How far above that first average' means the average of (rating avg length minus the overall average) over the remaining ratings. 'How far above the mean of the ratings that passed the first cut' means the average of (rating avg length minus the mean of the first-cut ratings' averages).
The 'mean of their own average lengths' is the unweighted mean of the per-rating averages for the ratings that passed the first cut.

alternatives.interpretation: The first 'average' is the unweighted mean of all five per-rating average lengths, not the overall film average.
